text:
jess_support: Customer hit a sudden 404 + param errors after upgrading our npm package to @redwood/inference-js@^0.19.0. They call embeddings and get 404 "/v1/embeds not found" then a schema error about unknown field 'model'. Node 18, repro attached.

alex_devex: Can you paste the minimal snippet they're using and the raw response body?

jess_support: Yup - posted below. They say it worked on 0.18.x and broke after bump.

```js
// customer code (TypeScript)
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const res = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'tiny-embed', input: ['a', 'b'] });
console.log(res);
```

Raw response (curl from their env):
```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": { "message": "Route '/v1/embeds' not found", "code": 404 } }
```

jess_support: After switching to direct HTTP they used: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -d '{"model_id":"tiny-embed","inputs":["a","b"]}'
```
and that worked. So looks like SDK is calling /v1/embeds and sending 'model'/'input' names.

alex_devex: That screams SDK -> API contract drift. We changed the public API param names in the last internal bump (model -> model_id, input -> inputs) and standardized the route to /v1/embeddings. Did we publish a package with old routing?

support-bot: Release note: @release-bot published @redwood/inference-js v0.19.0 2026-03-05 14:12 UTC (chore: cherry-pick hotfix routing).

tom_engineering: I pulled 0.19.0 locally — interestingly package.json has a build script that points at legacy router mapping for embeds -> /v1/embeds (should have been removed). Looks like the final cut didn't include runtime router map update. Repro steps:
1) npm i @redwood/inference-js@0.19.0
2) node -e "require('@redwood/inference-js')" and inspect client._endpointMap.embeds
3) call embeddings.create -> fails with 404

maya_oncall: Any auth differences? Customer uses Bearer token. They initially saw 404 then a second response: 400 with body: 
```
{ "error": { "message": "Unknown field: model", "code": "invalid_args" } }
```
so sometimes SDK route hit a gateway that expected new shape. Likely some requests are routed to new service and some to old, depends on region fallback.

alex_devex: Workaround for customers: pin to @redwood/inference-js@0.18.x or do a direct HTTP call and use model_id + inputs. We'll push a hotfix ASAP.

tom_engineering: Creating PR to revert routing map and add a compatibility flag in client constructor: 
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey, compatibility: 'legacy-0.18' });
```
But that's just temporary. I can also force-build 0.19.1 with correct endpoints.

jess_support: Customer asked if this could cause billing/duplicate charge retries — they do exponential retries on 5xx only. Here 404/400 won't be retried but they were concerned about partial writes. Confirmed no billing events were created since embedding calls are stateless (they only return vectors).

maya_oncall: Logging notes: we should search prod logs for inbound path '/v1/embeds' since the SDK leak might affect other customers. I'll run query for last 24h and flag accounts.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-embeds-sdk-mapping (assigned: @tom_engineering).

alex_devex: For now message to customers: apologize + advise pinning to 0.18.x or temporarily using REST with model_id/inputs. ETA for patch: 2 hours. I'll draft a short KB.

jess_support: Customer is fine with pin for immediate fix. They wanted repro notes I can send them. I'll include the curl examples and pin instructions.

tom_engineering: Patch published: @redwood/inference-js@0.19.1 with corrected endpoint map and additional unit tests (route compat). Also added an explicit deprecation warning in console when you run 0.18.x -> 0.19.x mismatches.

jess_support: Sent update to customer, they validated that 0.19.1 works in their staging. Closing on their side. :tada:
